title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare. They say your coverage will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use official-sounding language to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and bank information right now."
red_flags: Caller says your coverage will be canceled immediately
They ask for your Social Security or bank info
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text message saying there is a problem with a package delivery. The message asks you to click a link to fix the issue or pay a fee. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to update your address and pay the $1.50 fee."
red_flags: Link to click for payment or personal info
what_to_do: Do not click the link. Delete the message and check with the delivery company using their official website.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails that look like they are from the Social Security Administration. The email says there is a problem with your account and you need to click a link to fix it. The link goes to a fake site that steals your information.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Click here to verify your information or your benefits will be suspended."
red_flags: Email says your benefits will be suspended
Asks you to click a link and enter personal info
Email address is not from ssa.gov
what_to_do: Do not click any links. Go to the official Social Security website or call them if you are worried.

title: Romance Scams on Facebook
how_it_works: Someone you meet on Facebook or another social media site starts a friendly conversation. They quickly say they love you and ask for money, often for an emergency or travel. They may use fake photos and stories.
example_message: "I want to come visit you but my bank account is frozen. Can you send me $500 for a plane ticket?"
red_flags: Person you never met asks for money
They avoid video calls or meeting in person
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: You get a call from someone pretending to be your grandchild or a police officer. They say your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away for bail or an emergency. They ask you to keep it a secret.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need $2,000 for bail. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad!"
red_flags: Caller says it’s an emergency and asks for secrecy
They want money sent by wire or gift cards
They don’t sound quite like your grandchild
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.
